capitals.name: Phong Châu (Phú Thọ)
capitals.note: The 15th-century Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư places the capital at Phong Châu in present-day Phú Thọ Province; semi-legendary.

correction.text: 'geographically covering most of modern Northern Vietnam', the land of the Lạc Việt, capital at Phong Châu in Phú Thọ

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Văn Lang row; its Âu Lạc row starts -256 on the Red River delta and the Âu Việt hills). The Văn Lang page gives only a traditional chronology ('Văn Lang: 2524-258 BC', 88 Hùng Kings 'supposedly', 18 names recorded) and 'most of modern Northern Vietnam' with four borders (South China Sea, Ba Thục, Dongting Lake, Champa); the Đông Sơn page dates the culture 'from 1000 BC until the first century AD' and 'Vietnamese historians attribute the culture to the states of Văn Lang and Âu Lạc'. The start -1000 is the Đông Sơn date, not the page's 2524 BC. Neither page gives an area.

region.text: 'geographically covering most of modern Northern Vietnam', the land of the Lạc Việt, capital at Phong Châu in Phú Thọ

ledger.note: Dong Son bronze age: the Lac Viet of the Red River. The Đông Sơn page dates the culture 'from 1000 BC' and says 'Vietnamese historians attribute the culture to the states of Văn Lang and Âu Lạc'; the Văn Lang page's own chronology (Xích Quỷ 2879-2524 BC, Văn Lang 2524-258 BC) is traditional, so -1000 is a bridge to the archaeology (confidence 1). Some historians find 'no actual evidence' that the Đông Sơn people were Vietnamese.

ledger.note: c. 258 BCE: Thục Phán ends Văn Lang. 'Văn Lang ended c. 258 BC when the Âu invaded under their Shu prince Thục Phán'; 'Thục defeated the last Hùng Vương, united the kingdoms as Âu Lạc, and proclaimed himself An Dương Vương.' The au-lac dossier dates the founding 257 BCE.

sources.title: Đông Sơn culture
sources.note: Dating 1000 BC to the first century AD, centred on the Red River Delta, attribution to Văn Lang and Âu Lạc and the warnings against it.

notes: A semi-legendary state: the Văn Lang page gives a traditional chronology (2524-258 BC), the Hồng Bàng dynasty and 88 Hùng Kings; the Đông Sơn page calls the state attribution a view of Vietnamese historians and cites Taylor, Nguyen Phuong and Phan against it. The dossier is a placeholder to make au-lac's predecessor exist: start -1000 is the Đông Sơn date (confidence 1), the end -258 is the page's. The orchestrator may prefer a culture entry (type culture) or to start the state at 700 BCE if a better page is opened; no page I opened gives 700 BCE. The extent is 'most of modern Northern Vietnam' (Tonkin region) with four named borders; the Âu Lạc dossier draws a smaller Red River delta shape (Cliopatria -256). Nam Cương (Thục Phán's Âu Việt realm, named by se-01-a) is not written: no page of its own was opened. Wikidata unknown.
